column1:
A user reports they can browse the internet but cannot access internal resources like \\fileserver. What is the FIRST thing you check?

A. Reset the user password
B. Check the client’s DNS configuration
C. Reboot the file server
D. Disable the firewall
column2:
Correct Answer: B

Command to run:
ipconfig /all

What it checks:
Shows which DNS servers the client is using.

Why it works:
DNS determines how hostnames resolve to IPs. Internal resources require internal DNS.

Success:
DNS servers point to internal IPs (usually domain controllers).

Failure:
Public DNS, router IPs, or no DNS servers listed.

Common pitfall:
Assuming internet access means DNS is correct.

column1:
A domain-joined workstation cannot log in with domain credentials, but internet access works. Which command should you run FIRST?

A. nslookup
B. ping
C. ipconfig /all
D. ipconfig /flushdns
column2:
Correct Answer: C

Command to run:
ipconfig /all

What it checks:
DNS servers, gateway, adapter configuration.

Why it works:
Active Directory authentication depends on internal DNS.

Success:
DNS servers are internal DC IPs.

Failure:
DNS points to public or incorrect servers.

Common pitfall:
Resetting passwords before checking DNS.

column1:
A VPN user reports the VPN is connected but internal resources do not resolve. What should you check NEXT?

A. Antivirus status
B. DNS servers assigned to the VPN adapter
C. User permissions
D. Browser cache
column2:
Correct Answer: B

Command to run:
ipconfig /all

What it checks:
DNS servers associated with the VPN adapter.

Why it works:
VPNs must push internal DNS servers for name resolution.

Success:
Internal DNS listed on VPN adapter.

Failure:
Local or public DNS still used.

Common pitfall:
Assuming VPN connectivity guarantees internal access.

Internal DNS listed on VPN adapter.

Local or public DNS still used.

Assuming VPN connectivity guarantees internal access.

column1:
A user reports they can browse the internet but cannot access internal resources like \\fileserver. What is the FIRST thing you check?

A. Reset the user password
B. Check the client’s DNS configuration
C. Reboot the file server
D. Disable the firewall
column2:
Correct Answer: B

Command to run:
ipconfig /all

What it checks:
Shows which DNS servers the client is using.

Why it works:
DNS determines how hostnames resolve to IPs. Internal resources require internal DNS.

Success:
DNS servers point to internal IPs (usually domain controllers).

Failure:
Public DNS, router IPs, or no DNS servers listed.

Common pitfall:
Assuming internet access means DNS is correct.

column1:
A domain-joined workstation cannot log in with domain credentials, but internet access works. Which command should you run FIRST?

A. nslookup
B. ping
C. ipconfig /all
D. ipconfig /flushdns
column2:
Correct Answer: C

Command to run:
ipconfig /all

What it checks:
DNS servers, gateway, adapter configuration.

Why it works:
Active Directory authentication depends on internal DNS.

Success:
DNS servers are internal DC IPs.

Failure:
DNS points to public or incorrect servers.

Common pitfall:
Resetting passwords before checking DNS.
